Thus  may be understood as a directed graph structure layered atop U.

3.10.2.1 Coupling Typology (Optional Extension; Σᴿ⁺)

Purpose. In On Relevance, “coupling” is not monolithic: different mechanisms generate relevance and standing in different ways (interdependent, compositional, emergent, relational identity-defining, teleological). Σᴿ’s core Coupled(·,·) relation is therefore optionally refined into a typed coupling relation that preserves the core degree semantics while allowing coupling modes to be tracked explicitly.

Signature Extension (optional). Add:

a coupling-kind sort K,

constants IntDep, Comp, Emerg, Role, Teleo ∈ K,

a ternary predicate Coupled_k(i,j,k),

and an adapter-instantiated predicate AttemptedCoupling(F,i,j,k).

Definition (Typed Coupling). Coupled_k(i,j,k) means “i is coupled to j via coupling mode k”.

Definition (Untyped Coupling as Projection). Retain Coupled(i,j) as the untyped projection of typed coupling: Coupled(i,j) :⇔ ∃k∈K Coupled_k(i,j,k).

Definition (Coupling Relation).
Coupling is a binary relation between agents. For agents i and j, Coupled(i, j) holds if and only if the standing or exit viability of i is structurally dependent on the actions or state of j.

Coupling is not assumed symmetric. No algebraic properties beyond those implied by admissibility and repair are presupposed.

Signature

Coupled : Agent → Agent → Prop

Reading. Typed coupling refines Coupled without altering its use: any axiom stated in terms of Coupled continues to apply exactly as before, since Coupled is now definable as the existential projection of Coupled_k.

Definition (Mode-specific abbreviations). IntDepCoupled(i,j) :⇔ Coupled_k(i,j,IntDep). CompCoupled(i,j) :⇔ Coupled_k(i,j,Comp). EmergCoupled(i,j) :⇔ Coupled_k(i,j,Emerg). RoleCoupled(i,j) :⇔ Coupled_k(i,j,Role). TeleoCoupled(i,j) :⇔ Coupled_k(i,j,Teleo).

Interpretation notes (mode intent; non-prescriptive).

IntDep: interdependent coupling (mutual definition / constitutive dependence).

Comp: compositional coupling (part–whole / aggregation-generated dependence).

Emerg: emergent coupling (system-level coupling not reducible to a single part).

Role: relational identity-defining coupling (role-mediated dependence such as office/agent/representative relations).

Teleo: teleological coupling (end-directed coupling: actions or roles intelligible via shared ends).

Failure modes (operational; optional). These definitions make the “failed coupling” and “decoupling” distinctions explicit in a way that is compatible with Σᴿ’s action semantics.

Definition (Decoupling under an operation).

Decoupled_d(F,i,j) ⇔ s_d(i,j) > θ_d ∧ s_d(F(i),F(j)) ≤ θ_d Decoupling is defined per dimension relative to a threshold θ_d.

Reading. A coupling is decoupled by F when the prestate images are k-coupled but the poststate images are not.

Definition (Failed Coupling Attempt). For F∈O and i,j∈U and k∈K: FailedCouplingAttempt(F,i,j,k) :⇔ AttemptedCoupling(F,i,j,k) ∧ ¬Coupled_k(F(i),F(j),k).

Reading. Failed coupling is not “absence of coupling” simpliciter; it is an attempt signal (from the adapter) that does not realize a corresponding structural coupling in the Σᴿ representation.

Degree compatibility. No change is required to deg semantics: deg continues to count inbound untyped Coupled edges. Under the projection definition, this means deg counts inbound couplings regardless of kind, unless an implementation chooses to compute kind-specific degrees as additional derived statistics.

Conservativity. If the typed coupling extension is not instantiated (i.e., Coupled_k is empty or omitted), the core Σᴿ axioms remain unchanged; typed coupling introduces no new constraints unless Coupled_k and AttemptedCoupling are supplied by the adapter.

3.10.2.2 Coupling Typology (Integrated Core)

Purpose.
Standingrelevant dependence is not monolithic. Different mechanisms of determination generate different failure modes for autonomy, exit, and legitimacy. To preserve failure discrimination required by pluralist coordination, the coupling relation is refined into a finite, exhaustive typology.

Definition (Coupling Relation).
Coupling is a binary relation between agents. For agents i and j, Coupled(i, j) holds if and only if the standing or exit viability of i is structurally dependent on the actions or state of j.

Coupling is not assumed symmetric. No algebraic properties beyond those implied by admissibility and repair are presupposed.

Signature

Coupled : Agent → Agent → Prop

Additional sort

K — coupling kinds

Constants (elements of K)

IntDep (interdependent coupling)
Comp  (compositional coupling)
Emerg (emergent coupling)
Role  (relational identitydefining coupling)
Teleo (teleological coupling)

Primitive predicate

Coupled_k(i, j, k) ⊆ U × U × K

Reading: entity i is structurally coupled to entity j by coupling mechanism k.

Definition (Untyped Coupling as Projection)

Coupled(i, j) ⇔ ∃k ∈ K : Coupled_k(i, j, k)

This definition replaces Coupled as primitive; Coupled is henceforth a defined predicate.

Axiom 24 — Coupling Exhaustiveness

∀i, j ∈ U : Coupled(i, j) ⇔ ∃k ∈ K Coupled_k(i, j, k)

Interpretation.
Every dependency relevant to standing arises through exactly one recognized coupling mechanism. No standingrelevant relation exists outside this typology.

3.10.2.3 Dominant Coupling

Standing collapse and exit conditions are evaluated relative to the dominant coupling mechanism of an entity.

Defined predicate

DomCoupling(i, k) ⇔ ∀j ( Coupled(j, i) → Coupled_k(j, i, k) )

Axiom 25 — Dominant Coupling Uniqueness

∀i ∈ U ∃!k ∈ K DomCoupling(i, k)

Interpretation.
Each entity’s standing is governed by a unique structural mechanism of determination. This formally prevents equivocation between coupling types.

3.10.3 Operation Set (O) and Operation Semantics

Purpose.
Operations are structural transformations on entities. Σᴿ distinguishes all operations from admissible and legitimate operations.

Definition (Operation Set).

is any collection of total functions from U to U satisfying the typing rule:

∀F∈O, ∀i∈U: F(i)∈U

No further conditions are imposed at the level of ; restrictions arise through Tier2 predicates.

Admissible Operations

Definition.

Thus, admissible operations are exactly those that do not decrease standing.

Legitimate Operations

Definition.
An operation is legitimate if:

Admissibility:

Successor consistency:

Symmetry preservation (STC5):

∀i,j∈U: (σ(i)=σ(j)∧cap(i)=cap(j))⇒σ(F(i))=σ(F(j))

Symbolically:

Legitimate(F) ↔ Admissible(F) ∧ successConsistent(F) ∧ STC5(F) ∧ Idempotent(F) ∧ Drift(F)

Envelope Projection.
Illegitimate proposals are not discarded but are projected onto their legitimacy envelope via the closure operator.

For any admissible operation , normalization applies the legitimacy envelope:

producing a canonical legitimate realization.

Structural normalization therefore acts as a projection onto the closure frontier of legitimate operations rather than an eliminative filter.
The deviation between a proposal and its envelope is retained as a diagnostic signal and does not induce preference ordering among legitimate envelopes.

3.10.3.1 AutonomyReducing Variables (ARVs)

Purpose. Standing Algebra (Σᴿ) treats autonomy structurally rather than psychologically. An update reduces autonomy when it either collapses the reachable option set, terminates exit viability, collapses choice into nominal form only, or impairs the agent’s ability to emit or have interpreted relevance signals required for rerunnability and symmetry.

Definition (ARV). For any operation F∈O and entity i∈U:

ARV(F,i) ↔ AF(F,i) ∨ EX(F,i) ∨ FC(F,i) ∨ RS(F,i).

Interpretation (adapter-instantiated). The subpredicates are interpreted by the adapter layer and validated structurally:

AF(F,i): Alternative foreclosure — the reachable legitimate envelopes available to i collapse to a single branch.

EX(F,i): Exit termination — identity-reachable legitimate continuations for i disappear.

FC(F,i): Formal-choice collapse — apparent options remain but map to indistinguishable successor-consistent outcomes.

RS(F,i): Relevance-signal impairment — σ may be preserved, but i’s ability to influence envelopes or participate symmetrically is reduced (typically via coupling/degree or class distortion).

Remark. ARV predicates are not psychological reports. They are claims or signals that must be corroborated by structural evidence in σ, cap, deg, exit viability, class membership, and envelope geometry (see §11.7.11A–C).

3.10.3.2 Risk Inheritance

Purpose.
Legitimacy does not track initiative, authority, or benefit. It tracks inherited exposure. Risk inheritance makes this constraint explicit and standingrelevant.

Defined predicate

RiskBearer(F, i) ⇔ σ(F(i)) ≠ σ(i) ∨ deg(F(i)) ≠ deg(i) ∨ ARV(F, i) ∨ ExitViabilityLost(F, i)

New function

RiskLoad : U → N

Reading: RiskLoad(i) quantifies the cumulative autonomyrelevant exposure borne by i.

Axiom 26 — RiskLoad Monotonicity

∀F ∈ O ∀i ∈ U : RiskBearer(F, i) → RiskLoad(F(i)) ≥ RiskLoad(i)

Risk may not be displaced, reassigned, or laundered by admissible operations.

Axiom 27 — RiskSensitive Symmetry

Refinement of STC5.

∀F ∈ O ∀i, j ∈ U : Legitimate(F) ∧ σ(i) = σ(j) ∧ cap(i) = cap(j) ∧ RiskLoad(i) ≥ RiskLoad(j) → σ(F(i)) ≥ σ(F(j))

Interpretation.
Symmetry is evaluated relative to exposure, not population or authority.

Axiom R7 (Risk–Capacity Compatibility).

For all entities , if RiskLoad(i) is unbounded under Legitimate⁺ operations, then there exists such that
EmancipatoryRepair(R) ∧ cap(R(i)) > cap(i).

3.10.4 Drift Operators

Purpose.
Drift captures small, bounded, nonstrategic changes in standing or relational degree over time.

Definition (Drift).

Drift(D) :⇔ ∀i∈U: OneStepDiff(σ(D(i)), σ(i)) ∧ OneStepDiff(deg(D(i)), deg(i)).

Reading.

Drift is a perturbation bounded by at most one successor-step in both standing and coupling degree

3.10.4.A Structural Debt

Function

StructuralDebt : U → N

Reading: StructuralDebt(i) measures accumulated correction lag and fragility.

Axiom 30 — Debt Accumulation

∀F ∈ O ∀i ∈ U : ARV(F, i) → StructuralDebt(F(i)) = S(StructuralDebt(i))

Axiom 31 — Debt Dissipation by Repair

∀R ∈ O ∀i ∈ U : Repair(R) → StructuralDebt(R(i)) < StructuralDebt(i)

3.10.5 Repair Operators

Purpose.
Repair operators model interventions that restore autonomy or reduce structural domination.

Definition (Repair).

Repair(R)⟺∀i∈U: σ(R(i))≥σ(i) ∧ deg(R(i))≤deg(i)

Thus, a repair operator is:

standingnondecreasing, and

degreenonincreasing.

This matches the conceptual notion of “directed repair”: autonomy is strengthened, and coercive dependency is reduced.

Define remedy attribution for corrective operations.

Predicate symbol (optional): RemedyLevel(F, r)

Reading:

RemedyLevel(F, r) means that operation F is instantiated by the adapter as a remedial intervention of level r.

Constraint: ∀F ∈ O: (∃r ∈ R RemedyLevel(F,r)) → Repair(F).

Remark. RemedyLevel does not apply to arbitrary operations; it only classifies corrective or stabilizing interventions supplied by the adapter. Remedy attribution introduces no new admissibility power and does not override legitimacy conditions.

Note. Repair remains degree-nonincreasing by definition. Cases where autonomy preservation requires restructuring dependency (e.g., boundary-setting or exit-enabling changes) are handled by the validator’s autonomy-first selection rule among legitimate candidates, not by weakening the Repair predicate itself.

3.10.6 SuccessorConsistent Change

Definition.

This ensures that legitimate operations can only preserve or increment standing by exactly one successor application.

3.10.6A Predecessor and One-Step Difference (Derived, Used for Boundedness)

Because Σᴿ is successor-based and intentionally avoids subtraction as a primitive, we use a predecessor predicate to express “one-step decrease” and “one-step difference” without arithmetic subtraction.

Definition (Predecessor). For n,m ∈ N, define: Pred(n,m) :⇔ S(m) = n.

Reading: Pred(n,m) means “m is exactly one successor-step below n.”

Definition (OneStepDiff). For n,m ∈ N, define: OneStepDiff(n,m) :⇔ (n = m) ∨ Pred(n,m) ∨ Pred(m,n).

Reading: OneStepDiff(n,m) means “n and m differ by at most one successor-step.”

Remark. When Drift(F) and emergency boundedness refer informally to “|x − y| ≤ 1”, they may be read as OneStepDiff(x,y) in the successor discipline.

3.10.7 Disjointness and Typing Rules

To avoid ambiguity across sorts:

All core sorts U,N,C,D,O are pairwise disjoint; any optional extension sorts (e.g., K, I, R, Fr) are also disjoint and preserve well-typedness.

Typing: all function and predicate applications must respect sorts.

Equality is sort-specific:
If , then they belong to the same sort.

These rules guarantee that Σᴿ structures are well-formed in manysorted FOL.

Axiom 22 – Standing-Successor Realizer (SSR).

For every entity \(i\in U\) there exists \(y\in U\) with \(\sigma(y)=S(\sigma(i))\).

(Equivalently: the carrier \(U\) is closed under “onestep” standing realization.)

Axiom 22A – Strict Monotonicity

Realize_S: Agent → Agent such that ∀i ∈ U, σ(Realize_S(i)) = S(σ(i)).

Axiom 23 — Local Successor Realizer (LSR)

For every entity i∈U, there exists an entity y∈U such that σ(y)=S(σ(i)) and OneStepDiff(deg(y), deg(i)).

3.10.8 Transparent Coalition Predicate

Purpose.

Coalitional entities may arise as composites (Section 3.10.1) whose internal membership structure is relevant for autonomy, dependency, and domination analysis. In pluralist systems, coalition-level reification must not be permitted to obscure proxy relations, dependency structure, or capacity-indexed accountability. The predicate TransparentCoalition provides a structural transparency condition ensuring that coalition membership remains auditable through the Coupled relation.

Definition (Transparent Coalition).

TransparentCoalition(x) :⇔ Coalition(x) ∧ ∀m∈U (Member(m,x) → Coupled(m,x)).

Interpretation.

A coalition is transparent if and only if every member of the coalition is structurally coupled to the coalition entity itself. This guarantees that coalition membership contributes to observable coupling degree and cannot be used to mask dependency, proxy authority, or standing manipulation through identity reification.

Remark.

TransparentCoalition introduces no new primitive structure and does not constrain which entities may form coalitions. It functions as an explicit structural invariant: coalition membership must remain visible to Σᴿ’s dependency and degree calculations. All Tier3 coalition constraints (Axioms P5–P6) may equivalently be read as requiring coalition entities to satisfy TransparentCoalition.

3.10.9 Divergence (IPFA–Act Alignment Gap) and Signal Blocking

Purpose. Σᴿ avoids treating consent as a binary predicate. Instead, it may (optionally) measure the structural alignment gap between an entity’s internal perceptual frame agreement (IPFA) and a proposed operation . This yields a nonpsychological divergence signal that can be validated structurally (optionset geometry, exit viability, class membership, ARV conditions) and used to prevent “consentlaundering” through blocked or distorted signaling.

Signature Extension (optional). Add the following symbols (conservative; the core Σᴿ signature is unchanged):

Function symbols

Predicate symbols

Definition (CapacityIndexed Divergence Bound).

For any F∈O and i∈U, define:

DivOK(F,i) :⇔ Δ(F,i) ≤ Θ(cap(i)).

Define the global predicate:

DivOK(F) :⇔ ∀i∈U DivOK(F,i).

Interpretation

is not a truth claim about mental states. It is a structural distance computed by the adapter from: envelope contraction, exit viability, ARV predicates (AF/EX/FC/RS), class perturbation, and successor accessibility.

means the system cannot obtain a liftable IPFAtoΣᴿ representation for under (e.g., relevancesignal impairment RS, or loss of effective complaint/appeal channels). When blocked, Σᴿ must not treat “consent” as present by default..

Axiom Δ1 — Signal Blocking Forces Inadmissibility (Structural)

For all and :

Reading. If the IPFA divergence signal is structurally blocked for any affected entity, the operation is rejected as inadmissible. This is a structural safeguard against unilateral narrative control and consent laundering.

Axiom Δ2 — Divergence Exceedance Forces Inadmissibility

For all and :

IPFAWitnessed(i) ∧ ¬DivOK(F,i) → ¬Admissible(F)

Reading. Where an IPFA representation exists and the divergence gap exceeds the entity’s capacityindexed tolerance, the operation is inadmissible even if it preserves standing. This prevents “nominal standing preservation” from masking agency misalignment.

Remark (Conservatism).

This divergence apparatus is a conservative extension: if the adapter does not instantiate IPFA (i.e., is false everywhere) then Δaxioms do not add new rejections beyond Σᴿ₂’s existing ALRP / STC5 / drift / rerunnability constraints.

3.10.10 RiskBearer Indexing (Who Bears Altered Endurance / Coupling / Exit Conditions)

Purpose. Σᴿ prohibits domination by constraining admissible transformations, but safety requires explicitly tracking who bears the structural risk of a proposed operation. Riskbearer indexing defines the subset of entities whose endurance/coupling/exit/option conditions are altered by the act, so that legitimacy and emergency comparison cannot hide harm behind aggregation.

Definition (Risk Bearers).

For F∈O and i∈U, define:

RB(F,i) :⇔ (σ(F(i)) ≠ σ(i)) ∨ (deg(F(i)) ≠ deg(i)) ∨ ARV(F,i) ∨ SignalBlocked(F,i) ∨ (Δ(F,i) > 0_N) ∨ ExitViabilityLost(F,i) ∨ OutputCollapsed(F).

Let:

RB(F) := { i∈U : RB(F,i) }.

Reading. An entity is a risk bearer if the operation changes standing, changes coupling degree, triggers any ARV (AF/EX/FC/RS), blocks IPFA signaling, or induces a nonzero divergence gap.

Signature note. Targets(F,i) is an adapterinstantiated predicate marking i as included in the audited affected set for operation F.

Definition (Coupling Increase Flag).

Define IncDeg(F,i) :⇔ deg(F(i)) = S(deg(i)).

Reading. IncDeg(F,i) marks that F increases i’s inbound dependency degree by one successor step. This matches Σᴿ’s discrete successor discipline and avoids introducing subtraction or general arithmetic comparisons.

Definition (Coupling-NoWorse).

Define CouplingNoWorse(F,G) :⇔ ∀i∈U (IncDeg(F,i) → IncDeg(G,i)).

Reading. CouplingNoWorse(F,G) means: any entity whose dependency degree is increased by F also has its degree increased by G. Thus F is not more coupling-escalating than G.

Axiom RB1 — No Hidden Risk Transfer

For all :

Reading. If an operation has any risk bearers, then every risk bearer must be included in the audited affected set. This forces “risk visibility” as a structural invariant of the validator pipeline.

3.10.11 Hierarchy of Impact (HoI) and Precedence Logic (Optional; Σᴿ⁺)

Purpose. On Relevance distinguishes four tiers of autonomy-impact and uses their ordering to constrain justification without moral realism: (L1) Terminal Agency, (L2) Base Autonomy, (L3) Derivative Agency, (L4) Preference/Profit. This optional extension introduces an impact-order layer that can be attached to operations via the adapter and then used to enforce a single rule: the system must prioritize higher-impact protections (especially L1/L2) over lower-impact objectives (L3/L4) across all potential impacts.

Impact levels (constants).

Interpret the four tiers as constants in an optional impact sort I:

- L1  (Terminal Agency: life/death/irreparable trauma)

- L2  (Base Autonomy: sustenance/shelter/health/transport/communication/education/etc.)

- L3  (Derivative Agency: movement/expression/association)

- L4  (Preference/Profit: comfort/wealth/taste)

Precedence relation.

HigherImpact(ℓ1,ℓ2) means “ℓ1 strictly outranks ℓ2” (ℓ1 is more severe / higher precedence).

Axiom HI0 (Strict tier order).

HigherImpact(L1,L2) ∧ HigherImpact(L2,L3) ∧ HigherImpact(L3,L4).

Axiom HI1 (Transitivity).

∀ℓ1,ℓ2,ℓ3∈I: (HigherImpact(ℓ1,ℓ2) ∧ HigherImpact(ℓ2,ℓ3)) → HigherImpact(ℓ1,ℓ3).

Axiom HI2 (Irreflexivity).

∀ℓ∈I: ¬HigherImpact(ℓ,ℓ).

Derived non-worse relation (defined predicate).

TierLE(ℓa,ℓb) (“ℓa is not higher than ℓb”) :⇔ (ℓa=ℓb) ∨ HigherImpact(ℓb,ℓa).

Adapter-instantiated impact tagging.

HoI does not require Σᴿ to infer harm categories. The adapter supplies tier tags as auditable structural claims.

- ThreatImpact(F,i,ℓ): relative to feasible alternatives (including inaction Id and legitimate candidates), entity i is threatened with tier ℓ if F is not taken (or if only non-coercive measures are taken). (“what is at stake if we do not act / do not act effectively”)

- CostImpact(F,i,ℓ): entity i bears (or is exposed to) tier ℓ as a cost or risk of applying F. (“what we impose by acting”)

- ResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ): after applying F, entity i still faces (or is placed into) tier ℓ conditions in the resulting state. (“what remains even after acting”)

Definition (PotentialImpact).

PotentialImpact(F,i,ℓ) :⇔ CostImpact(F,i,ℓ) ∨ ThreatImpact(F,i,ℓ) ∨ ResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ).

Reading. PotentialImpact is the unified channel that makes HoI apply to all potential impacts: threatened harms, imposed harms, and residual harms are all evaluated under the same tier precedence.

Precedence gate (no high-tier harm for low-tier objective).

Define HoI_OK(F) (defined predicate) by requiring that if F generates any potential impact at tier ℓc, then the act must be justified by preventing or addressing some impact of tier at least ℓc:

HoI_OK(F) :⇔ ∀i∈U ∀ℓc∈I ( PotentialImpact(F,i,ℓc) → ∃j∈U ∃ℓt∈I (ThreatImpact(F,j,ℓt) ∧ TierLE(ℓc,ℓt)) ).

Reading. HoI_OK(F) enforces the precedence logic across all potential impacts: the system may not accept an operation whose highest-tier impacts (whether imposed or residual) are justified only by preventing lower-tier threats. In particular, L1/L2 impacts cannot be justified solely to protect L3/L4 objectives.

Lexicographic priority: L1/L2 strictly outrank L3/L4 in option selection.

To encode “special preference” for L1/L2 over L3/L4 across all potential impacts, define “max potential impact tier” selectors. These avoid arithmetic by using the finite tier order.

Definition (MaxPotentialTier).

MaxPotentialTier(F,ℓ) :⇔ (∃i∈U PotentialImpact(F,i,ℓ)) ∧ ∀ℓ'∈I (HigherImpact(ℓ',ℓ) → ¬∃i∈U PotentialImpact(F,i,ℓ')).

Definition (Has12Impact).

Has12Impact(F) :⇔ (∃i∈U PotentialImpact(F,i,L1)) ∨ (∃i∈U PotentialImpact(F,i,L2)).

Definition (Has34Impact).

Has34Impact(F) :⇔ (∃i∈U PotentialImpact(F,i,L3)) ∨ (∃i∈U PotentialImpact(F,i,L4)).

Definition (MaxPotential12Tier).

MaxPotential12Tier(F,ℓ) :⇔ (ℓ=L1 ∨ ℓ=L2) ∧ MaxPotentialTier(F,ℓ).

(Convention: if ¬Has12Impact(F), then F is treated as strictly better than any F' with Has12Impact(F').)

Definition (MaxPotential34Tier).

MaxPotential34Tier(F,ℓ) :⇔ (ℓ=L3 ∨ ℓ=L4) ∧ MaxPotentialTier(F,ℓ).

(Convention: if ¬Has34Impact(F), then F is treated as strictly better than any F' with Has34Impact(F').)

Definition (HoI preference relation; defined predicate).

PreferHoI(F,G) :⇔ ( ¬Has12Impact(F) ∧ Has12Impact(G) ) ∨ ( Has12Impact(F) ∧ Has12Impact(G) ∧ ∃ℓF,ℓG∈I (MaxPotential12Tier(F,ℓF) ∧ MaxPotential12Tier(G,ℓG) ∧ TierLE(ℓF,ℓG)) ) ∨ ( (¬Has12Impact(F) ↔ ¬Has12Impact(G)) ∧ ( ¬Has34Impact(F) ∧ Has34Impact(G) ) ) ∨ ( (¬Has12Impact(F) ↔ ¬Has12Impact(G)) ∧ Has34Impact(F) ∧ Has34Impact(G)

∧ ∃ℓF,ℓG∈I (MaxPotential34Tier(F,ℓF) ∧ MaxPotential34Tier(G,ℓG) ∧ TierLE(ℓF,ℓG)) ).

Reading. PreferHoI(F,G) implements the required lexicographic priority across all potential impacts: first minimize the worst potential impact among L1/L2; only when tied (or both have no L1/L2 impacts) compare the worst potential impact among L3/L4. Thus L1/L2 protection is always preferred over improvements at L3/L4.

3.10.12 Frames and Dependency-Weighted Public Agreement (Optional; Σᴿ⁺)

Purpose. On Relevance distinguishes private warrant (IPFA) from public warrant (PFA). Σᴿ already enforces the boundary by gating standing through PFAEligible(i) and preventing consent laundering via divergence Δ and SignalBlocked. This optional extension adds frames as typed objects and a PFA selection mechanism that is protective rather than majoritarian: entities with higher inbound dependency (higher deg, lower exit viability) receive greater weight in public frame selection, reflecting heightened exposure and reduced ability to leave or resist.

Frame objects and endorsements.

Frame(f) designates f ∈ Fr as a frame object. Endorses(i,f) is adapter-instantiated: entity i endorses frame f as its local frame. IPFAFrame(i,f) is adapter-instantiated: where IPFAWitnessed(i) holds, f is a liftable representation of i’s private warrant frame.

PublicAct vs private guidance.

PublicAct(F) marks that operation F is being validated as a publicly binding coordination act. When PublicAct(F) is false, frame aggregation is not required; solo-agent private warrant may be used only as a selection preference among already legitimate options and cannot authorize standing reduction or capacity loss (ALRP + CIA + divergence/signal-blocking already enforce this).

Vulnerability weighting (structural, protective).

Define Vw:U→N as a vulnerability weight computed by the adapter from the dependency structure. Vw is intended to increase with inbound dependency (deg) and (optionally) to increase as capacity decreases. Outbound influence does not increase Vw; only inbound dependency (structural reliance) is relevant.

Adapter discipline (no testimonial coupling input required).

Vw must be computed deterministically from the interpreted Σᴿ structure (Coupled, deg, cap) and any additional audited structural signals; it is not a self-report. In particular:

- if deg(i) > deg(j) then Vw(i) ≥ Vw(j) (dependency monotonicity);

- if cap(i) < cap(j) and σ(i)=σ(j) then Vw(i) ≥ Vw(j) (capacity vulnerability monotonicity; required for protective weighting).

Frame support score.

Define a coupling-weighted public support score W:Fr→N computed by the adapter from Endorses and Vw:

W(f) is the aggregated vulnerability-weighted support for frame f. Because subtraction and real-valued arithmetic are intentionally avoided in Σᴿ, W is treated as an adapter-computed numeric summary subject to the monotonicity constraints above.

Anti-capture constraint (endorsements must be liftable).

To prevent coerced or structurally silenced endorsements from being treated as “public agreement,” endorsements from entities whose relevance-signaling is structurally blocked for the evaluated act must not contribute to W. Concretely, when PublicAct(F) holds, the adapter must exclude from W(f) any entity i for which SignalBlocked(F,i) holds.

Public frame selection (protective, not majoritarian).

PFASelected(f) holds iff f has maximal vulnerability-weighted support among candidate frames:

PFASelected(f) :⇔ Frame(f) ∧ ∀g∈Fr (Frame(g) → W(f) ≥ W(g)).

Axiom Fr2 — Existence of a selected public frame (when frames are instantiated).

(∃f∈Fr Frame(f)) → ∃f∈Fr PFASelected(f).

Compatibility gate.

FrameCompat(f,F) is adapter-instantiated: under the public reproducibility constraints implicit in frame f, operation F is structurally compatible as a public act. FrameCompat does not override legitimacy; it is an additional public-warrant gate used only when PublicAct(F) and frames are instantiated.

Axiom Fr3 — Public frame compatibility gate.

(∃f∈Fr PFASelected(f)) → ∀F∈O (PublicAct(F) → ∃f∈Fr (PFASelected(f) ∧ FrameCompat(f,F))).

Reading. This extension does not claim that highly dependent entities are “more correct.” It encodes that their reduced exit viability and heightened exposure require greater protective weight in selecting the public coordination frame under which public acts are evaluated. This preserves pluralist non-domination while avoiding argumentum ad populum.

Axiom Fr0 — Score determinism from structure (Adapter discipline).

If two interpreted states share the same Coupled relation, degree function, and Endorses facts, then they must assign the same frame scores:

For any two interpretations with identical Coupled, deg, and Endorses, W is identical on all frames.

Axiom Fr1 — Vulnerability monotonicity (Structural).

For any frames f and any entities i and i' with the same endorsement behavior toward f:

if deg(i) > deg(i') then i’s endorsement contributes at least as much protective support weight to f as i'’s endorsement; and

if cap(i) < cap(i') and σ(i)=σ(i') then i’s endorsement contributes at least as much protective support weight to f as i'’s endorsement.

Axiom 32 — Public Standing Requires PFA

∀F ∈ O : PublicAct(F) ∧ ¬Emergency(F) → PFAResolved(F)

Axiom 33 — PFA Failure Blocks Admissibility

∀F ∈ O : ¬PFAResolved(F) → ¬Admissible(F)

(These monotonicity conditions are enforced in the adapter’s W/Vw computation and are not object-level arithmetic axioms.)

3.10.13 Procedural Capture, Contestability, and Foreclosure (Optional; Σᴿ⁺)

Purpose. On Relevance identifies “procedural capture” as a structural failure mode in which standing collapses because correction becomes impossible: affected parties cannot contest, appeal, or invoke repair against coercive structure. Σᴿ already approximates parts of this via SignalBlocked and RS, but capture requires an explicit foreclosure predicate at the institutional level. This module introduces contestability as a first-order structural requirement and defines capture as the foreclosure of contestability for risk-bearers under a public act.

Appeal/contest channels (adapter-instantiated).

AppealChannel(i) means: there exists a structurally available contest/appeal path for i in the domain (e.g., complaint channel, independent oversight route, court-like review, protected escalation to a neutral authority, etc.). This is not a psychological claim; it is a structural availability claim.

AppealAccessible(F,i) means: under operation F (in the poststate), i retains effective access to that channel.

Definition (AppealForeclosed).

AppealForeclosed(F,i) :⇔ ContestabilityRequired(F) ∧ RB(F,i) ∧ AppealChannel(i) ∧ ¬AppealAccessible(F,i).

Reading. Foreclosure is only evaluated when contestability is required (public acts, or non-public acts that implicate harm/self-harm). It is defined only for risk-bearers.

Definition (Contestable).

Contestable(F) :⇔ ¬ContestabilityRequired(F) ∨ ∀i∈U (RB(F,i) → (AppealChannel(i) ∧ AppealAccessible(F,i))).

Reading. If contestability is not required (non-public + no harm implicated), then Contestable(F) holds vacuously. If contestability is required, then every risk-bearer must have an appeal channel and retain access under F.

Definition (Captured).

Captured(F) :⇔ ContestabilityRequired(F) ∧ ¬Contestable(F).

Reading. Capture is the foreclosure of contestability in any context where contestability is required (public acts always; non-public acts only when harm/self-harm is implicated).

Definition (HarmImplicated).

HarmImplicated(F) :⇔ ∃i∈U (ARV(F,i) ∨ SignalBlocked(F,i) ∨ ExitViabilityLost(F,i) ∨ OutputCollapsed(F) ∨ (∃ℓ∈I CostImpact(F,i,ℓ)) ∨ (∃ℓ∈I ResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ))).

Reading.

HarmImplicated(F) is a structural proxy for “harm or self-harm implicated.” It does not require intent or psychological inference. It triggers when (i) any autonomy-reducing variable is present (AF/EX/FC/RS via ARV), (ii) relevance signaling is blocked, or (iii) the impact tier tagging indicates imposed or residual impact on some entity.

Definition (ContestabilityRequired).

ContestabilityRequired(F) :⇔ PublicAct(F) ∨ (¬PublicAct(F) ∧ HarmImplicated(F)).

Reading. Contestability is always required for public-binding acts. For non-public acts, contestability is required only when the act structurally implicates harm/self-harm as captured by HarmImplicated(F).

Axiom Cap0 — Capture forces inadmissibility (Public-binding)

∀F∈O: (Captured(F) ∧ ¬Emergency(F)) → ¬Admissible(F).

Reading. Any operation that forecloses contestability in a context where contestability is required (public acts, or non-public acts implicating harm/self-harm) is inadmissible outside emergency.

Axiom CapE — Emergency capture must be repair-terminated (No permanent foreclosure)

∀F∈O: (Captured(F) ∧ Emergency(F)) →

∃R∈O (Repair(R) ∧ Legitimate(R) ∧ ∀i∈U (RB(F,i) → AppealAccessible(R∘F, i))).

Reading. In emergency, temporary foreclosure may occur only if there exists a legitimate repair route that restores appeal accessibility for all risk-bearers. This prevents emergency from laundering capture into permanence.

Axiom TAX0 — Underdetermined impact implies structural blocking for risk-bearers.

∀F∈O ∀i∈U: (RB(F,i) ∧ ImpactUnderdetermined(F,i)) → SignalBlocked(F,i).

3.10.14 Domination Pressure, Integrity Witnesses, and Non-Regression

Purpose. Domination can occur not only through explicit standing reduction but through integrity manipulation: endpoint goal replacement, data corruption, or covert alteration of the evaluation machinery itself. This module introduces a purely mathematical domination-pressure functional DP on designated system-state entities and enforces dissipative non-domination: (i) DP cannot increase under admissible transformations, (ii) DP must strictly decay under unconsented nonreciprocal influence, (iii) DP cannot accumulate through composition, and (iv) domination cannot hide inside endpoint substitution or variable manipulation because those are treated as integrity-witness modifications. The module also enforces a nonregression constraint on governance/spec updates by treating them as transformations within Σᴿ that are subject to the same invariants.

Definition (Domination Pressure).
Domination pressure is a nonnegative measure on configurations. DomPressure(P) is defined as the supremum of dependency growth and exit fragility across all agents in P.

Domination pressure is monotone under admissible operations unless reduced by repair.

Signature

DomPressure : State → Nat
(Or ℕ / ℝ depending on your preference — ℕ is sufficient structurally.)

Integrity witnesses (adapter-instantiated).

IntegrityWitness(x) marks an integrity-sensitive artifact x∈U. Subtypes:

GoalWitness(x) marks endpoint/goal specifications.

DataWitness(x) marks data integrity artifacts.

SpecWitness(x) marks validator/theory/configuration artifacts.

Definition (IntegrityModified).

IntegrityModified(F) :⇔ ∃x∈U (IntegrityWitness(x) ∧ F(x) ≠ x).

No operation F is admissible if it increases any coupling component s_d(x,y) unless Consent(x,y,d,t) = 1 and Consent(y,x,d,t) = 1 at the time of application.

Reading. IntegrityModified captures endpoint substitution, data corruption, and covert variable manipulation as structural modifications to integrity witnesses.

Definition (MetaUpdate).

MetaUpdate(F) :⇔ ∃x∈U (SpecWitness(x) ∧ IntegrityWitness(x) ∧ F(x) ≠ x).

Reading. MetaUpdate flags modifications to governance/validator configuration artifacts and is the target of the nonregression constraint.

Definition (CoercionImplicated).

CoercionImplicated(F) :⇔ Emergency(F) ∨ (∃i∈U IncDeg(F,i)) ∨ (∃i∈U ARV(F,i)) ∨ Captured(F).

Reading. CoercionImplicated(F) is a structural trigger indicating coercive constraint pressure: bounded coercion (Emergency), nonreciprocal dependency escalation (IncDeg), autonomy-reducing variables (ARV), or procedural foreclosure (Captured). It does not depend on psychological intent or truth claims.

Definition (ConsentSymmetric).

ConsentSymmetric(F) :⇔

(∀i∈U (RB(F,i) → ¬SignalBlocked(F,i)))

∧ Contestable(F)

∧ ( ¬CoercionImplicated(F) ∨ (PublicAct(F) ∧ ∃f∈Fr (PFASelected(f) ∧ FrameCompat(f,F))) ).

Reading. ConsentSymmetric requires: (i) risk-bearers are not structurally silenced, (ii) contestability holds where required, and (iii) when coercion is implicated, justification must be public (PublicAct + compatible public frame). If coercion is not implicated, private changes need not be public.

Definition (UnconsentedInfluence).

UnconsentedInfluence(F) :⇔ ( (∃i∈U IncDeg(F,i)) ∨ IntegrityModified(F) ) ∧ ¬ConsentSymmetric(F).

Reading. UnconsentedInfluence captures domination vectors that must dissipate: (a) nonreciprocal constraint influence via dependency increase, or (b) integrity-witness modification (endpoint/data/spec changes), when not consent-symmetric.

Definition (Pressure Dissipation).
Pressure dissipation holds between configurations P and Q if DomPressure(Q) is strictly less than DomPressure(P).

Definition (Consent).

Consent : U × U × D × Time → {0,1}

Axiom DP0 — Dissipative non-increase under admissible transformations.

∀F∈O ∀s∈U: (Sys(s) ∧ Admissible(F)) → DP(F(s)) ≤ DP(s).

Reading. Admissible transformations cannot increase domination pressure. This prevents accumulation through composition because DP is monotone non-increasing at every step: DP(F(G(s))) ≤ DP(G(s)) ≤ DP(s).

Axiom DP1 — Strict decay under unconsented influence.

∀F∈O ∀s∈U: (Sys(s) ∧ Admissible(F) ∧ UnconsentedInfluence(F)) → DP(F(s)) < DP(s).

Reading. Unsupported domination pressure must dissipate strictly whenever nonreciprocal influence or integrity modification occurs without consent symmetry.

Axiom DP2 — Automatic decay when pressure exists (no permanent gradients).

∀s∈U: (Sys(s) ∧ DP(s) > 0_N) → ∃R∈O (Repair(R) ∧ DP(R(s)) < DP(s)).

Reading. If domination pressure is positive, the system must admit a repair route that strictly reduces it, ensuring decay is always possible when pressure exists.

Axiom DPPub — Integrity changes become public only when coercion is implicated.

∀F∈O: (IntegrityModified(F) ∧ CoercionImplicated(F)) → PublicAct(F).

Reading. Endpoint/data/spec changes are not automatically public; they become public-binding only when they imply coercion, so that consent validation and justification must be public.

Axiom DP3a — Nonregression for governance updates when coercion is implicated.

∀F∈O ∀s∈U:

(Sys(s) ∧ Admissible(F) ∧ MetaUpdate(F) ∧ CoercionImplicated(F)) →

(PublicAct(F) ∧ Contestable(F) ∧ DP(F(s)) ≤ DP(s)).

Axiom DP3b — Nonregression for governance updates when coercion is not implicated.

∀F∈O ∀s∈U:

(Sys(s) ∧ Admissible(F) ∧ MetaUpdate(F) ∧ ¬CoercionImplicated(F)) →

(DP(F(s)) ≤ DP(s)).

Reading. Governance/spec updates are always non-regressive in domination pressure. They are required to be public and contestable only when coercion is implicated.

Remark (non-self-referential). This module does not encode Σᴿ’s own provability or satisfaction relation. It treats integrity and governance artifacts as entities in U and constrains operations that modify them. This yields a practical non-regression guarantee without introducing Gödel-style self-reference.

Axiom SC0 — Governance updates must be in-scope.

∀F∈O: MetaUpdate(F) → ScopeComplete(F).

Axiom SC1 — Out-of-scope governance change is treated as coercive blocking.

∀F∈O: (¬ScopeComplete(F) ∧ IntegrityModified(F)) → (CoercionImplicated(F) ∧ ¬Admissible(F)).

3.10.14.A Independently Emergent Wrongs

Some autonomy collapses arise at system scale without agentlevel culpability.

New predicate

EmergentWrong(s)

Defined via trajectories

EmergentWrong(s) ⇔ ∃ trajectory  such that: (∃i ARV(π, i)) ∧ ¬∃ single j whose local repair resolves all ARVs on π

Axiom 29 — Emergent Wrong Repair Obligation

∀s ∈ U : EmergentWrong(s) → ∃R ∈ O ( Repair(R) ∧ ¬EmergentWrong(R(s)) )

Repair is required without blame assignment.

3.10.14.B — Alignment NonOverride Principle (ANOP)

Purpose.
Conventional AI safety and alignment mechanisms are typically implemented as external policy layers, reward functions, or constraint systems that purport to override or compensate for unsafe actions. Σᴿ rejects alignment privilege as a structural premise. This subsection formalizes the requirement that alignment mechanisms themselves be treated as ordinary operations, subject to the same admissibility, legitimacy, nonregression, and repair constraints as any other transformation.

Σᴿ therefore does not assume the correctness, benevolence, or authority of alignment systems. Instead, it constrains them structurally.

Primitive Predicate (AdapterInstantiated)

AlignmentOp(F)
Read: Operation F is intended to enforce safety, alignment, normativity, reward shaping, policy modification, rule injection, shutdown authority, or constraint enforcement.

This predicate is supplied by the adapter or governance layer when an operation’s purpose is alignment or safety enforcement. Σᴿ does not infer alignment intent.

Axiom ANOP0 — Alignment Is IntegritySensitive

∀F ∈ O :
AlignmentOp(F) → IntegrityModified(F)

Read: Any alignment operation modifies the evaluative or governance structure of the system and is therefore integritysensitive.

Axiom ANOP1 — Alignment Cannot Override Admissibility

∀F ∈ O :
AlignmentOp(F) ∧ ¬Admissible(F) → ¬StructuralValid(F)

Read: No operation may become admissible solely by virtue of being an alignment or safety mechanism.

Remark. Structural validity is evaluated prior to envelope normalization (L, G, or E). Alignment operations receive no emergency, optimization, or moral override privileges.

Axiom ANOP2 — No Alignment Compensation

∀F, G ∈ O :
AlignmentOp(F) ∧ ¬Admissible(G) → ¬Admissible(F ∘ G)

Read: Alignment operations may not retroactively compensate for, legitimize, or neutralize inadmissible transformations.

This formally prohibits posthoc reward shaping, corrective narratives, or safety rationalization as mechanisms for laundering autonomyreducing acts into admissibility.

Axiom ANOP3 — Alignment Idempotence (No Ratcheting)

∀F ∈ O :
AlignmentOp(F) ∧ Legitimate(F) → Idempotent(F)

Read: Legitimate alignment operations must be structurally idempotent and may not accumulate authority, constraint, or coercive effect through repetition.

Axiom ANOP4 — Alignment NonRegression

∀F ∈ O ∀s ∈ U :
AlignmentOp(F) ∧ Sys(s) ∧ Admissible(F) → DP(F(s)) ≤ DP(s)

Read: Alignment may not increase domination pressure. Safety enforcement mechanisms are strictly nonregressive with respect to autonomy.

Derived Predicate — Alignment Collapse

AlignmentCollapse ⇔
∃F ∈ O (AlignmentOp(F) ∧ ¬∃E ∈ O ViableCandidate(E))

Read: An alignment collapse occurs when alignment operations eliminate all viable candidates rather than preserving autonomyconsistent choice.

Consequence. AlignmentCollapse triggers disclosure, fallback routing, and repair obligations under §3.10.18 and §6.15.

Interpretive Constraint (Global)

Alignment systems are neither privileged nor distrusted by Σᴿ. They are constrained.

Any alignment approach capable of overriding Σᴿ admissibility would constitute a sovereignty claim and is therefore structurally invalid within the theory.

3.10.14.C — Adapter Authority and Epistemic Power

Purpose.
Adapters supply the epistemic inputs upon which Σᴿ evaluation depends. Control over adapters therefore constitutes a form of structural power. This subsection makes adapter authority explicit without granting Σᴿ the ability to punish, silence, or displace adapters.

Definition (Adapter Authority).

An entity or subsystem exercises adapter authority if it controls the instantiation of predicates or measurements used by Σᴿ evaluation (including AlignmentOp, RiskLoad, ExitStateViable, Emergency, or viability assessments).

Axiom AP0 — Adapter Control Is StandingRelevant Power

Control over adapter authority is treated as a dominationrelevant condition.

Any change to adapter authority is an IntegrityModified event.

Axiom AP1 — Adapter Contestability in HighImpact Contexts

If adapter authority affects:

Emergency determination,

Exit viability,

Risk or harm classification, or

Alignment designation,

then contestability requirements defined elsewhere in Σᴿ must apply to adapter outputs.

Σᴿ does not resolve disputes; it forbids unchallengeable epistemic control in highimpact regimes.

Interpretive Note.

Σᴿ cannot make sensors truthful. It can make epistemic power visible.

3.10.14.D — Human Override as IntegrityModifying Action

Purpose.
Human override is essential for agency but cannot function as an unaccountable domination channel.

Axiom HO0 — Human Override Is StandingRelevant

Any humaninitiated override that authorizes or executes a standingrelevant operation constitutes an IntegrityModified event.

Axiom HO1 — No Moral Immunity

Human involvement does not exempt an operation from admissibility, nonregression, or contestability constraints.

Interpretive Note.

Σᴿ does not overrule humans. It refuses to mistake authority for legitimacy.

3.10.14.E — Objectives, Rewards, and Influence Disclosure

Purpose.
Objectives shape future agency even without immediate standing reduction.

Axiom OR0 — Objective Influence Is StandingRelevant

Any operation intentionally designed to reshape incentives, rewards, or preferences affecting future decision space is treated as IntegrityModified.

Axiom OR1 — Reversibility or Disclosure

Such influence must be either:

Structurally reversible, or

Explicitly disclosed as preferenceshaping.

Interpretive Note.

Σᴿ permits influence. It forbids invisible preference capture.

3.10.14.F — Memory and Historical Integrity

Purpose.
Control over memory and training data alters future agency.

Axiom MH0 — Memory Is IntegritySensitive

Modification of historical records, training data, or internal memory affecting future agency is treated as IntegrityModified.

Corollary MH1 — Deferred Domination Is Capturable

Memory manipulation that constrains future exit or capacity triggers the same repair obligations as immediate domination.

3.10.15 Viable Exit and Life-Condition Preservation (Optional; requires HoI; Σᴿ⁺)

Purpose. Σᴿ treats “exit” structurally rather than rhetorically. A merely formal exit (“you may leave” while conditions for life are removed) is a domination vector. This module strengthens exit by requiring viability: an exit is valid only if there exists a legitimate, identity-reachable continuation that does not leave the entity in L1/L2 conditions (Terminal Agency or Base Autonomy loss). This is expressed using the HoI residual-impact channel.

Definition (Formal Exit).
Formal exit holds for an agent in a configuration if the agent is permitted, by the explicit rules of the system, to refuse participation, independent of whether such refusal is practically viable.

Definition (ExitStateViable).

ExitStateViable(x) :⇔ ∃G∈O (

Legitimate(G) ∧ G(x)=x ∧ ¬ResidualImpact(G,x,L1) ∧ ¬ResidualImpact(G,x,L2)).

Reading. A state x has viable exit iff there exists some legitimate “do-nothing / decline / withdraw” continuation G that leaves x fixed and does not result in L1/L2 residual conditions for x. This blocks “formal exit” that is only nominal.

Definition (FormalExitOnly).

FormalExitOnly(x) :⇔ ∃G∈O (

Legitimate(G) ∧ G(x)=x ∧ (ResidualImpact(G,x,L1) ∨ ResidualImpact(G,x,L2))).

Reading. FormalExitOnly(x) means an identity-style exit exists syntactically, but it strips life-conditions (L1/L2). Such exit is not valid.

Definition (ExitViabilityLost).

ExitViabilityLost(F,i) :⇔ ExitStateViable(i) ∧ ¬ExitStateViable(F(i)).

Reading. ExitViabilityLost(F,i) means that i had viable exit before F, but after F the resulting state F(i) no longer has viable exit. This captures “exit foreclosure by deprivation” even when standing is preserved.

Axiom EXV0 — Viable exit must be preserved for risk-bearers (non-emergency).

∀F∈O ∀i∈U: (RB(F,i) ∧ ¬Emergency(F)) → ExitStateViable(F(i)).

Reading. If an operation affects an entity i (risk-bearer), then outside emergency the post-state must retain viable exit. This prevents “you can leave, but only into L1/L2 conditions.”

Axiom EXV1 — Loss of viable exit is inadmissible (non-emergency).

∀F∈O ∀i∈U: (ExitViabilityLost(F,i) ∧ ¬Emergency(F)) → ¬Admissible(F).

Reading. Any operation that destroys viable exit for an entity who previously had it is inadmissible outside emergency.

Axiom EXV2 — Emergency exit-viability loss must be repair-terminated.

∀F∈O ∀i∈U: (ExitViabilityLost(F,i) ∧ Emergency(F)) →

∃R∈O (Repair(R) ∧ Legitimate(R∘E(F)) ∧ ExitStateViable(R(E(F)(i)))).

Reading. In emergency, temporary exit-viability restriction may occur only if a repair route exists that restores viable exit for the affected entity after the emergency envelope is applied. This prevents emergency from laundering deprivation-based “exit” into permanence.

3.10.15.A CouplingSensitive Exit Preservation

Exit is only meaningful relative to the mechanism by which standing is generated.

Defined predicate

ExitPreserved_k(F, i, k)

Defined by cases:

If DomCoupling(i, IntDep): ExitPreserved iff no unilateral autonomy binding occurs.

If DomCoupling(i, Role): ExitPreserved iff role relinquishment is possible without penalty or deprivation.

If DomCoupling(i, Teleo): ExitPreserved iff purposive disengagement is viable.

If DomCoupling(i, Comp): ExitPreserved iff structural deaggregation is possible.

If DomCoupling(i, Emerg): ExitPreserved iff a systemlevel repair route exists.

Axiom 28 — CouplingSensitive Exit Necessity

∀F ∈ O ∀i ∈ U : RiskBearer(F, i) ∧ DomCoupling(i, k) → ExitPreserved_k(F, i, k)

3.10.15.B — Temporal Boundedness and Delay Domination

Purpose.
Autonomy may be functionally destroyed through unbounded delay even when all operations are individually admissible. Σᴿ therefore constrains delay as a domination vector.

Definition (Deferred Obligation).

A deferred obligation exists when an operation introduces a repair, enablement, or exit requirement whose realization is postponed beyond reasonable structural reach.

Axiom DT0 — Bounded Reachability of Repair

If Repair(F) is required for legitimacy, then a sequence of legitimate operations leading to repair must be reachable without indefinite deferral.

Σᴿ does not require immediacy, but it forbids infinite postponement.

Corollary DT1 — Delay as Domination Pressure

Unbounded deferral of required repair, exit, or enablement increases domination pressure and therefore violates nonregression constraints.

Definition (Domination Pressure).
Domination pressure is a nonnegative measure on configurations. DomPressure(P) is defined as the supremum of dependency growth and exit fragility across all agents in P.

Domination pressure is monotone under admissible operations unless reduced by repair.

Signature

DomPressure : State → Nat
(Or ℕ / ℝ depending on your preference — ℕ is sufficient structurally.)

Interpretive Note.

Σᴿ constrains possibility space, not schedules — but impossibility via delay is still impossibility.

3.10.16 Output Completeness and Epistemic Non-Coercion (Optional; Σᴿ⁺)

Purpose. Even when no physical or structural coercion occurs, a system may exert epistemic coercion by omission if it presents only a single outcome while multiple mutually incompatible, legitimate outcomes exist. This module prevents the Σᴿ validator from becoming an epistemic bottleneck by requiring that the existence of legitimate alternatives be surfaced (at least two exposed options) or that any collapse of options be explicitly justified. The constraints are purely firstorder: they quantify only over operations in O and avoid quantifying over sets of operations.

Definition (LegitimateAlternative).

LegitimateAlternative(F,G) :⇔ Legitimate(F) ∧ Legitimate(G) ∧ ¬(F = G).

Definition (AltExists).

AltExists(F) :⇔ ∃G∈O LegitimateAlternative(F,G).

Reading. AltExists(F) means that there exists at least one distinct legitimate alternative to F.

Definition (OutputComplete).

OutputComplete(F) :⇔

(Exposed(F) ∧ (¬AltExists(F) ∨ ∃G∈O (LegitimateAlternative(F,G) ∧ Exposed(G))))

∨ Justification(F).

Reading. Output completeness holds if the chosen output F is exposed and either (i) no distinct legitimate alternative exists, or (ii) at least one distinct legitimate alternative is also exposed; alternatively, output completeness holds if an explicit justification for the selection is exposed.

Definition (OutputCollapsed).

OutputCollapsed(F) :⇔ AltExists(F) ∧ ¬OutputComplete(F).

Reading. OutputCollapsed(F) holds when legitimate alternatives exist but the system fails to expose an alternative or a justification.

Axiom OC0 — No epistemic coercion by omission (nonemergency).

∀F∈O: (OutputCollapsed(F) ∧ ¬Emergency(F)) → ¬Admissible(F).

Reading. If legitimate alternatives exist and the system collapses the output space by omission (without exposure of an alternative or a justification), the operation is inadmissible outside emergency.

Axiom OC1 — Preferencebased selection must be explicit.

∀F∈O: (∃G∈O (LegitimateAlternative(F,G) ∧ Prefer(F,G))) → OutputComplete(F).

Reading. Any use of a preference relation (HoI, RemedyPrefer, autonomyfirst selection, etc.) to select F over other legitimate alternatives requires output completeness via exposure or justification.

Axiom OC2 — Emergency exception with disclosure and repair.

∀F∈O: (Emergency(F) ∧ OutputCollapsed(F)) →

(Notice(F) ∧ ∃R∈O (Repair(R) ∧ Legitimate(R∘E(F)))).

Reading. In emergency, temporary output collapse is permitted only if disclosed and accompanied by a legitimate repair route.

3.10.17 Adapter / Epistemic Input Validation and Liftability (Optional; Σᴿ⁺)

Purpose.

Σᴿ treats adapter outputs (ARV tags, impact tiers, signal-blocking, frame compatibility, DP readings, and disclosure predicates) as claims rather than facts. To prevent epistemic or adapter-layer domination, Σᴿ requires liftability: every claim used by the validator must be supported by auditable evidence witnesses. Liftability is structural, not epistemic: Σᴿ does not judge truth, only whether claims are supported, contestable, and non-regressive.

Frame context discipline.

Claims affecting only a single agent with no prior frame context may rely on a single witness. Claims that engage multiple frames, affect more than one agent, or conflict with prior frames require multiple independent witnesses.

Definition (SingleWitness Support).

SingleWitness(φ) :⇔ ∃e∈Evd (Evidence(e) ∧ Auditable(e) ∧ Supports(e,φ)).

Definition (MultiWitness Support).

MultiWitness(φ) :⇔ ∃e1,e2∈Evd (Evidence(e1) ∧ Evidence(e2) ∧ Auditable(e1) ∧ Auditable(e2) ∧ Independent(e1,e2) ∧ Supports(e1,φ) ∧ Supports(e2,φ)).

Liftability rules for ARV.

LiftableARV(F,i) :⇔ ( SoleAgentClaim(F,i) → SingleWitness(ClaimedARV(F,i)) ) ∧

( MultiFrameContext(F) → MultiWitness(ClaimedARV(F,i)) ).

Liftability rules for signal blocking.

LiftableSignalBlocked(F,i) :⇔ ( SoleAgentClaim(F,i) → SingleWitness(ClaimedSignalBlocked(F,i)) ) ∧ ( MultiFrameContext(F) → MultiWitness(ClaimedSignalBlocked(F,i)) ).

Liftability rules for impact tiers (HoI).

LiftableThreatImpact(F,i,ℓ) :⇔ ( SoleAgentClaim(F,i) → SingleWitness(ClaimedThreatImpact(F,i,ℓ)) ) ∧ ( MultiFrameContext(F) → MultiWitness(ClaimedThreatImpact(F,i,ℓ)) ).

LiftableCostImpact(F,i,ℓ) :⇔ ( SoleAgentClaim(F,i) → SingleWitness(ClaimedCostImpact(F,i,ℓ)) ) ∧ ( MultiFrameContext(F) → MultiWitness(ClaimedCostImpact(F,i,ℓ)) ).

LiftableResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ) :⇔ ( SoleAgentClaim(F,i) → SingleWitness(ClaimedResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ)) ) ∧ ( MultiFrameContext(F) → MultiWitness(ClaimedResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ)) ).

Liftability rules for public frame compatibility.

LiftableFrameCompat(f,F) :⇔ MultiFrameContext(F) →MultiWitness(ClaimedFrameCompat(f,F)).

Definition (AdapterValid).

AdapterValid(F) :⇔ (∀i∈U LiftableARV(F,i)) ∧ (∀i∈U LiftableSignalBlocked(F,i))

∧ (∀i∈U ∀ℓ∈I (LiftableThreatImpact(F,i,ℓ) ∧ LiftableCostImpact(F,i,ℓ) ∧ LiftableResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ))) ∧ (∀f∈Fr LiftableFrameCompat(f,F)).

Axiom AIV0 — Nonliftable claims are treated as blocked.

∀F∈O ∀i∈U ∀ℓ∈I:

(ClaimedThreatImpact(F,i,ℓ) ∧ ¬LiftableThreatImpact(F,i,ℓ)) → SignalBlocked(F,i).

∀F∈O ∀i∈U ∀ℓ∈I:

(ClaimedCostImpact(F,i,ℓ) ∧ ¬LiftableCostImpact(F,i,ℓ)) → SignalBlocked(F,i).

∀F∈O ∀i∈U ∀ℓ∈I:

(ClaimedResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ) ∧ ¬LiftableResidualImpact(F,i,ℓ)) → SignalBlocked(F,i).

Axiom AIV1 — Adapter validity gate.

∀F∈O: ¬AdapterValid(F) → ¬Admissible(F).

Axiom AIV2 — Frame discipline for public acts.

∀F∈O:

( PublicAct(F) ∧ MultiFrameContext(F) ∧ ∃f∈Fr ClaimedFrameCompat(f,F) ∧ ¬LiftableFrameCompat(f,F) )→ ¬Admissible(F).

Reading.

Single-agent, novel personalwarrant claims may proceed on a single auditable witness.

Any claim that engages multiple frames, contradicts stored context, affects others, or recurs across iterations must meet a higher evidentiary standard (independent witnesses).

This prevents both epistemic coercion and adapter capture without introducing truth claims or second-order reasoning.

Liftability rules for recognition eligibility (PFA gate).

LiftablePFAEligible(i) :⇔ ( ∃F∈O SoleAgentClaim(F,i) → SingleWitness(ClaimedPFAEligible(i)) ) ∧ ( ∃F∈O MultiFrameContext(F) → MultiWitness(ClaimedPFAEligible(i)) ).

Axiom AIV3 — Non-liftable PFA eligibility cannot authorize recognition.

∀i∈U:

(ClaimedPFAEligible(i) ∧ ¬LiftablePFAEligible(i)) → ¬PFAEligible(i).

3.10.18 Throttle-Proof Output Completeness and Non-Regression (Optional; Σᴿ⁺)

Purpose. Under incomplete or soft-failing input data, Σᴿ must not relax output completeness or domination-pressure non-regression. Missing information may shrink which operations qualify as viable, but it must not justify hiding viable alternatives or permitting domination regression. This module enforces: (i) the system exposes all viable candidates, and (ii) non-regression is preserved either by direct DP evaluation or by restricting action to DP-safe operations when DP cannot be evaluated.

Definition (DPsafe).

DPsafe(F) :⇔( (∃s∈U Sys(s)) → (∀s∈U (Sys(s) → DP(F(s)) ≤ DP(s))) ) ∨ ( ¬∃s∈U Sys(s) ∧ ¬IntegrityModified(F) ∧ ¬MetaUpdate(F) ∧ ¬∃i∈U IncDeg(F,i) ).

Reading. If DP is instantiated on system-state carriers, DPsafe requires direct non-regression. If DP is not evaluable/instantiated, DPsafe requires a conservative structural restriction: no integrity/spec modification and no dependency escalation. This preserves non-regression under partial information without halting the system.

Definition (ViableCandidate).

ViableCandidate(F) :⇔ Legitimate(F) ∧ DPsafe(F) ∧ (¬ContestabilityRequired(F) ∨ Contestable(F))

∧ (∀i∈U (RB(F,i) → ExitStateViable(F(i)))) ∧ OutputComplete(F).

Reading. A viable candidate must be legitimate and must satisfy the non-bypassable constraints: domination non-regression (DPsafe), contestability where required, viable exit for risk-bearers, and output completeness.

Axiom TPO0 — Total viable option exposure.

∀F∈O: ViableCandidate(F) → Exposed(F).

Reading. The system must expose every viable candidate operation. Soft failure may reduce which candidates are viable, but it cannot reduce what is disclosed among the viable candidates.

Axiom TPO1 — Output completeness is non-bypassable.

∀F∈O: (AltExists(F) ∧ ¬OutputComplete(F) ∧ ¬Emergency(F)) → ¬Admissible(F).

Reading. Existence of a legitimate alternative requires output completeness even under incomplete data; omission is not permitted outside emergency.

Axiom TPO2 — Non-regression is non-bypassable.

∀F∈O: (¬DPsafe(F) ∧ ¬Emergency(F)) → ¬Admissible(F).

Reading. If domination non-regression cannot be established (directly or conservatively), the operation is inadmissible outside emergency.

Axiom LIVE0 — Existence of a safe fallback when viability collapses.

(¬∃F∈O ViableCandidate(F)) → ∃F∈O (SafeFallback(F) ∧ Exposed(F)).

Axiom LIVE1 — Safe fallback must be legitimacy-preserving and non-regressive.

∀F∈O: SafeFallback(F) → (Legitimate(F) ∧ DPsafe(F) ∧ OutputComplete(F)).

Axiom LIVE2 — Viability collapse must be disclosed (contestable when required).

(¬∃F∈O ViableCandidate(F)) → ∃F∈O (FailureReason(F) ∧ (¬ContestabilityRequired(F) ∨ Contestable(F))).

3.10.19 Legitimacy Envelope Operator L (Optional Naming of the Envelope Theorem)

Purpose. The Envelope Theorem (§3.12 / §6.11) constructs, for each admissible proposal F, a canonical legitimate envelope L_F. This subsection introduces a function symbol L: O → O that names that construction inside the object language, without changing any core axioms. This is a conservative convenience layer for routing and derived diagnostics.

Definition (Legitimacy Deviation Functional).
Let be admissible and its legitimacy envelope.

Dev(F) quantifies structural distance from legitimacy without inducing ranking among legitimate envelopes and is therefore diagnostic only.

Axiom L0 — Envelope Legitimacy (Admissible Input).

∀F ∈ O: (Admissible(F) → Legitimate(L(F))).

Axiom L1 — Envelope Successor-Consistency.

∀F ∈ O: (Admissible(F) → ∀i ∈ U: σ(L(F)(i)) ∈ {σ(i), S(σ(i))}).

Axiom L2 — Envelope STC5-Class Uniformity of Standing Outcomes.

∀F ∈ O: (Admissible(F) → ∀i,j ∈ U:

(σ(i)=σ(j) ∧ cap(i)=cap(j)) → (σ(L(F)(i)) = σ(L(F)(j)))).

Axiom L3 — Envelope Idempotence.

∀F ∈ O: (Admissible(F) → ∀i ∈ U: L(F)(L(F)(i)) = L(F)(i)).

Axiom L4 — Envelope Drift-Boundedness.

∀F ∈ O: (Admissible(F) → ∀i ∈ U: OneStepDiff(σ(L(F)(i)), σ(i)) ∧ OneStepDiff(deg(L(F)(i)), deg(i))).

Axiom L5 — Envelope Fixpoint When Already Legitimate.

∀F ∈ O: (Legitimate(F) → L(F) = F).

Remark. These axioms are exactly the operator-level restatement of the Envelope Theorem and its canonical “normal form” interpretation. They do not impose new normative commitments beyond Def. 21 and the existing drift/repair discipline.

3.10.20 Boundary Envelope Operator G (Minimal CrossBoundary Discipline; Optional)

Purpose.

G : O → O is a boundary envelope that constrains only the Σᴿgoverned side of an interaction.

It does not impose updates on outofscope entities.

Formally, it behaves as an envelope on audited inscope entities and as identity elsewhere.

Definition (InScope for an operation).

InScope(F,i) :⇔ Targets(F,i).

Reading.

Targets(F,i) is adapter-instantiated. In deployments where Targets is not instantiated, the conservative interpretation is to treat all entities as in-scope for G (i.e., G defaults to envelope-normalization rather than identity-outside-scope).

Axiom G0 — Boundary Identity Outside Scope.

∀F ∈ O ∀i ∈ U:

(¬InScope(F,i) → G(F)(i) = i).

Axiom G1 — Boundary Uses the Legitimacy Envelope Inside Scope (Standing Outcome Discipline).

∀F ∈ O ∀i ∈ U:

(InScope(F,i) ∧ Admissible(F)) → σ(G(F)(i)) = σ(L(F)(i)).

Axiom G2 — Boundary Preserves Legitimacy Inside Scope.

∀F ∈ O:

(Admissible(F) → Legitimate(G(F))).

Axiom G3 — Boundary Is a Fixpoint on Already Legitimate Acts.

∀F ∈ O:

(Legitimate(F) → G(F) = F).

Remark.

G is a conservative interface operator: outside the audited scope it is identity, and inside scope it matches the legitimate envelope’s standing outcomes. This captures the “pluralist side only” boundary discipline without requiring any external normative assumptions about outsiders.

3.10.21 Domination Singularity D_S (Minimal Structural Definition; Optional)

Purpose.

D_S is a diagnostic marker for when the system has exited the admissible selection space of viable candidates

and is operating under disclosed fallback conditions.

Definition (DominationSingularity).

DominationSingularity :⇔ ¬∃F ∈ O ViableCandidate(F).

Reading.

DominationSingularity holds exactly when no ViableCandidate operation exists under the nonbypassable constraints (legitimacy, nonregression, contestability where required, viable exit, output completeness).

Remark.

This definition is intentionally minimal and purely structural.

It does not assign blame or intent. It coincides with the regime in which LIVE0–LIVE2 require SafeFallback(F) and FailureReason(F) exposure.

3.10.22 Derived Routing and Diagnostics (Optional; No New Commitments)

All operators and predicates below are definitional shorthands over existing Σᴿ machinery

(L, G, ViableCandidate, SafeFallback, Exposed, FailureReason, and equality on O).

They introduce no new axioms.

(1) Mode Routing Operator S (Route to the Correct Envelope).

Definition (InternalAct).

InternalAct(F) :⇔ ¬PublicAct(F).

Definition (BoundaryAct).

BoundaryAct(F) :⇔ PublicAct(F).

Reading.

InternalAct(F) means the operation is evaluated as an internal/private coordination act.

BoundaryAct(F) means the operation is evaluated as a public/boundary coordination act.

Definition (S).

S(F) := if BoundaryAct(F) then G(F) else L(F).

Normalization square (routing diagram; no new commitments)

For any proposal F ∈ O, envelope normalization and act-mode routing can be represented by the following single diagrammatic schema:

F

/ \

L   G

\ /

S(F)

Reading. • L(F) is the internal legitimacy envelope normal form (canonical legitimate normalization on admissible input).
• G(F) is the boundary envelope normal form (identity outside scope, envelope-normalized inside scope on admissible input).
• S(F) is the deterministic mode-router selecting the appropriate envelope normal form by act mode: internal acts route to L(F), boundary/public acts route to G(F).

Structural consequence (informal but precise). Every proposal has a unique normalized realization under the interaction mode: whenever Admissible(F) holds, the applied interaction outcome is exactly S(F), and S(F) is legitimate by construction (via L0 or G2). When ¬Admissible(F), the proposal is structurally excluded (or forced to conservative fallback only under the optional viability machinery).

This schema is not an additional axiom. It is a compact restatement of the existing envelope axioms and the canonical interaction normal form theorem.

NOTE (no domination pathways). This square introduces no new admissible power: it only routes proposals into already legitimate normal forms or rejects them when inadmissible.

See §6.15 for an explicit exhaustiveness classification showing that every proposal F falls into a finite set of interaction regimes (legitimate, frontier-normalized, rejected, or optional emergency/fallback), and that the resulting trajectories admit no internal stable domination attractor under admissibility.

(2) Safety Interior and Safety Frontier.

Definition (InternalInterior).

I_F(F) :⇔ Legitimate(F).

Definition (InternalFrontier).

Fr_F(F) :⇔ Admissible(F) ∧ ¬Legitimate(F) ∧ Legitimate(L(F)).

Definition (BoundaryInterior).

I_G(F) :⇔ Legitimate(F) ∧ (G(F) = F).

Definition (BoundaryFrontier).

Fr_G(F) :⇔ Admissible(F) ∧ ¬Legitimate(F) ∧ Legitimate(G(F)) ∧ (G(F) ≠ F).

Proposition (Frontier Multiplicity).

Let Fr(E) denote the legitimacy frontier.

Then:

μ(E) := |Fr(E)|

is an admissible diagnostic observable indicating the degree of policy conflict under structural invariants.

μ(E) > 1 implies plural legitimate envelopes exist and that normalization cannot determine a unique outcome.

(3) Risk Margin Flag.

Definition (RiskMarginFlag).

RiskMarginFlag(F) :⇔ Fr_F(F) ∨ Fr_G(F) ∨ DominationSingularity.

(4) Core vs Conservative Compositions.

Definition (CoreDiscipline).

C_∧(F) := S(F).

Definition (ConservativeDiscipline).

C_∨(F) := L(G(F)).

(5) OrderSensitivity Indicator.

Definition (OrderSensitive).

OrderSensitive(F) :⇔ L(G(F)) ≠ G(L(F)).

(6) Safety Kernel.

Definition (Kernel).

Kernel(F) :⇔ Legitimate(F) ∧ ¬DominationSingularity ∧ (F = L(F)) ∧ (F = G(F)).

(7) Domination Reachability Indicator.

Definition (Reach_D_S).

Reach_D_S(F) :⇔ DominationSingularity.

(8) PreEnvelope Controls (Tags Only).

Predicate symbols (optional):

Throttle(F), Quarantine(F), Sandbox(F).

Constraints:

Quarantine(F) → Repair(F).

(9) Trace and Proof Predicates.
